recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Do not alter the base Range datatype for FHIR-5500; any future comparator support should remain tied to separate work-group decisions such as the Observation.referenceRange-specific FHIR-51566 change.
issue_request: FHIR-5500 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 MnM ballot comment asking what the Range datatype note meant by a "range flag" on low or high, because neither Range nor Quantity had such a property. The final resolution clarified that the obsolete Quantity element had become comparator.
initial_application: The issue was directly applied in commit 1dbbca6b115568107edc4dbfae0f0d483d9a44b5, which changed Range invariant wording from "No Range flag on Quantity" to "No Comparator flag on Quantity" and corrected the low.comparator path. Later source organization preserved that correction.
additional_context: Range and SimpleQuantity are active normative datatypes in source/fhir.ini. Current Range.low and Range.high are SimpleQuantity, and SimpleQuantity has a comparator.empty()/comparator.max=0 rule. Later FHIR-51566 allowed comparators only for Observation.referenceRange.low/high by changing those elements from SimpleQuantity to Quantity with explicit constraints; it did not reverse the base Range rule.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The obsolete "range flag" wording is absent from current active Range source, the implementer-facing narrative says comparator, and the current datatype model still enforces no comparators on base Range boundaries.

related_jiras.note: Later Quantity reorganization moved active Range and Quantity definitions into separate datatype spreadsheets and preserved the SimpleQuantity/no-comparator model.
Later OO decision allowed comparators for Observation.referenceRange by changing those elements from SimpleQuantity to Quantity, confirming that base Range comparator prohibition remains intentional.
